claims.text: Hallucinations in summaries compromise the factual accuracy of summaries.
Hallucinations in summaries lead to diminished user satisfaction.
The proposed framework employs a Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation (Q-S-E) methodology to enable quantitative detection of hallucinations.
The framework incorporates an iterative hallucination resolution mechanism to enhance the transparency of the modification process.
The framework incorporates an iterative hallucination resolution mechanism to improve the faithfulness of text summarization.
The proposed approach markedly improves the factual consistency of summaries on CNN/Daily Mail, PubMed, and ArXiv datasets.
The proposed approach preserves the informational completeness of summaries.

evidence.description: Experimental results on three benchmark datasets CNN/Daily Mail, PubMed, and ArXiv demonstrate that our approach markedly improves the factual consistency of summaries.
Experimental results demonstrate the approach preserves informational completeness while improving factual consistency.

methodologies.name: Q-S-E Framework
methodologies.description: A hallucination detection and mitigation framework using Question-Answer Generation, Sorting, and Evaluation with an iterative resolution mechanism.

limitations.text: Existing methods exhibit limitations in effectively detecting and mitigating hallucinations.
Existing methods often lack transparency in their underlying mechanisms.
